questions.q: What is the function of the eyepiece (ocular lens) in a light microscope?
a: To magnify the primary image formed by the objective lens, typically by 10x
To focus light directly onto microscope slides
To hold glass slides firmly in place on the stage
To adjust the color temperature of illumination

questions.q: Which part of a light microscope holds the objective lenses and can be rotated to change magnification power?
What is the primary function of the objective lenses on a compound light microscope?
a: To collect light passing through the specimen and form the first magnified real image
To measure the exact thickness of cell walls

questions.q: Which microscope knob is used for large, rapid adjustments to focus the specimen, especially when using low-power objective lenses?
Which knob is used for making very small, precise focus adjustments, particularly when viewing specimens under high power?
What is the purpose of the microscope stage clips?
a: To hold the glass microscope slide securely in position on the stage

questions.q: What is the function of the diaphragm or iris located beneath the microscope stage?
a: To control the amount and intensity of light passing up through the specimen
To cool down electric light bulbs

questions.q: Where does the light source (mirror or electric lamp) direct light during microscopy?
a: Upward through the aperture in the stage, through the slide and specimen

questions.q: How do you calculate the total magnification of a light microscope image?
a: Multiply the eyepiece magnification power by the objective lens magnification power
Add the eyepiece power to the objective power
Divide the objective power by the eyepiece power

questions.q: If a microscope has a 10x eyepiece and a 40x objective lens, what is the total magnification of the specimen?
What is the correct initial step when focusing a specimen under a light microscope?
a: Start with the highest power objective and coarse focus quickly
Start with the lowest power objective lens and focus using the coarse adjustment knob
Look through the eyepiece while turning the coarse knob upward rapidly
Remove the eyepiece lens to see better

questions.q: Why must you never use the coarse adjustment knob when viewing a specimen under high power (e.g., 40x objective)?
a: It makes the image too bright
It can drive the objective lens too far down, crushing the glass slide and scratching the expensive lens

questions.q: What term describes the ability of a microscope to distinguish between two distinct points that are close together, making details clear and sharp?
What is a major advantage of light microscopes over electron microscopes in school laboratories?
a: They can achieve millions of times higher magnification
They can be used to view live specimens in color and are affordable and portable
They require a vacuum chamber to operate
They use magnetic fields instead of glass lenses

questions.q: How does the image of a specimen appear when viewed through a standard compound light microscope compared to how it sits on the stage?
What is the purpose of placing a coverslip gently at an angle onto a wet mount slide before viewing?
a: To glue the specimen permanently to the desk
To prevent air bubbles from getting trapped and to protect the objective lens from liquid contact

questions.q: What is a biological stain (such as iodine solution or methylene blue) used for when preparing microscope slides?
a: To make transparent or colorless cellular structures (like nuclei or cell walls) clearly visible by adding contrast
To dissolve plant cell walls completely
To kill all bacteria on the desk

questions.q: What is the field of view in microscopy?
a: The metal arm supporting the body tube
The circular area of the specimen visible through the microscope eyepiece
The maximum weight the stage can hold
The distance between the objective lens and the slide

questions.q: If you move a microscope slide to the left while looking through the eyepiece, in which direction does the image appear to move?
a: It does not move at all

questions.q: What is the formula used to calculate the actual size of a biological specimen when given the image size and magnification?
a: Actual size = Magnification multiplied by Image size
Actual size = Image size plus Magnification
Actual size = Magnification divided by Image size
Actual size = Image size divided by Magnification

questions.q: An animal cell image measures 50 mm across in a drawing, and the magnification is 500x. What is the actual size of the cell?
Why is thin sectioning of biological specimens (like onion epidermis or leaf tissue) necessary for light microscopy?
a: To allow light to pass through the specimen so internal structures can be seen clearly
To increase the weight of the slide
To prevent slides from drying out

questions.q: What cleaning material should be used exclusively to clean delicate glass microscope lenses?
What is the function of the mirror or illuminator switch on a microscope?
a: To provide illumination for viewing the specimen

questions.q: What is the arm of a light microscope used for?
a: To support the body tube and serve as a safe handle when carrying the microscope
To hold glass slides on the stage

questions.q: What is the base of a microscope designed to do?
a: Provide stable, heavy support for the entire microscope structure

questions.q: What happens to the brightness of the field of view when you switch from a low-power objective lens (e.g., 4x) to a high-power objective lens (e.g., 40x)?
a: The field of view becomes much brighter
The field of view becomes darker, requiring adjustment of the diaphragm or light source

questions.q: What is a micrometre (μm) used for in biological measurements?
a: Measuring the height of whole plants
Measuring the speed of moving protozoa
Measuring microscopic structures like cell lengths and organelles

questions.q: How many micrometres (μm) are equivalent to 1 millimetre (mm)?
What is the primary role of the body tube in a compound microscope?
a: To maintain the correct distance and alignment between the eyepiece lens and the objective lenses

questions.q: Why should you keep both eyes open when looking down a monocular microscope eyepiece, with practice?
a: To keep track of laboratory exits
To prevent eye strain and fatigue during long observation sessions

questions.q: What term describes the stage platform on a microscope that allows precise movement of slides using mechanical control knobs?
When putting away a light microscope at the end of a practical, what should be left in position over the stage?
a: The lowest power objective lens clicked into place
The highest power 40x objective lens lowered fully

questions.q: What is the function of a microscope pointer inside an eyepiece?
a: To point out and identify specific features or cells in the field of view

questions.q: Why is immersion oil sometimes used with ultra-high magnification oil-immersion objective lenses in advanced biology?
a: To minimize light refraction (bending) and improve resolution at high magnification

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a simple microscope and a compound microscope?
a: Simple microscopes use electricity, compound ones do not
Simple microscopes have two stages, compound ones have one
Simple microscopes use digital screens, compound ones use mirrors
Simple microscopes use only one lens (like a magnifying glass), whereas compound microscopes use a system of multiple lenses

questions.q: What should you do if dust or a smudge is visible on the eyepiece lens while viewing a slide?
a: Clean it gently with clean lens paper
Scratch it off with a metal needle
Wipe it with a dirty laboratory coat sleeve
Ignore it and increase light intensity

questions.q: Why is it important to start focusing with the stage raised as high as possible (looking from the side) before lowering it with the coarse adjustment?
a: To prevent the objective lens from crashing downward into the glass slide during focusing
To test the stage spring clips

questions.q: What does a scale bar on a micrograph represent?
a: The date the photo was taken
A reference line of known actual size used to calculate real dimensions of magnified structures
The magnification power of the camera

questions.q: What is an electron microscope capable of showing that standard light microscopes cannot?
a: Live swimming protozoa in full color
Large plant tissues and whole leaves
Sub-cellular ultrastructure such as ribosomes, internal mitochondrial membranes, and viruses at extreme magnification
